faqs: How much does custom software development cost?

It is hours times rate. Upwork lists $40 to $70 an hour for intermediate developers and $70 to $150 or more for experts. A hypothetical 800 hour build costs $32,000 to $56,000 at the intermediate band and $56,000 to $120,000 at the expert band.
How much does a software developer cost per hour?

On Upwork, the median band is $10 to $100 an hour, with entry level at $20 to $40, intermediate at $40 to $70 and expert at $70 to $150 or more. A US software developer earns a median of $135,980 a year (BLS, May 2025), about $65.38 an hour on our conversion, or about $93 with benefits on our estimate.
How much does a web app cost to build?

The same hours times rate method applies. BLS puts the median web developer wage at $92,650 a year (May 2025), about $44.54 an hour on our arithmetic. Web apps with back end work may also need software developer rates, $40 to $150+ an hour on Upwork for intermediate to expert.
Is it cheaper to hire a freelancer or an in-house developer?

Per hour, Upwork's intermediate band of $40 to $70 is below our loaded estimate of about $93 for a US employee. An employee costs about $194,000 a year on that estimate whether or not there is work, while a freelancer is paid for the hours you buy.

Hours. Upwork names project complexity, developer experience, technology stack, project duration and location as the cost factors. Scope changes add hours too: 50 extra hours cost $2,000 to $3,500 at the intermediate band.
Should I build custom software or use a white-label platform?

Build when the workflow is your edge or no platform does it. HighLevel's plans are $97, $297 and $497 a month, so a year of its Pro plan ($5,964) equals about 64 loaded developer hours. A platform gives you its features rather than your own.
body:
Short answer. Custom software development costs $40 to $70 an hour for an intermediate freelance developer and $70 to $150 or more for an expert, going by Upwork's own rate page (read November 25, 2026). A US employee costs about $93 an hour once benefits are added, our arithmetic on the BLS median wage of $135,980 (May 2025). So the total is hours times rate: a hypothetical 800 hour build lands between $32,000 and $120,000 at Upwork's intermediate and expert rates.

There is no standard price list for "custom software", because every build is a different number of hours. What is public is the rate side: marketplace rates, government wage data and employer cost data. This guide puts those together, shows the arithmetic, and ends with a way to budget your own project. If a platform you can rebrand would do the job, compare it first with our guide to white-label SaaS on GoHighLevel.

Custom software development cost per hour

Upwork and two BLS datasets set the hourly range. Upwork runs the marketplace it reports on, so it has a stake in these numbers, and its footnote says the rates come from "certain historical contracts worldwide" and that what clients pay is negotiated.

RouteHourly costSource
Upwork, median band across developers$10 to $100Upwork rate page
Upwork, entry level$20 to $40Upwork rate page
Upwork, intermediate$40 to $70Upwork rate page
Upwork, expert$70 to $150+Upwork rate page
US employee, median wage onlyabout $65.38BLS, $135,980 / 2,080 hours
US employee, with benefitsabout $93our estimate from BLS ECEC

The employee rows are our arithmetic, explained in the in-house section below. The BLS figure is a median, so half of US software developers earn more and half earn less.

What a custom software project costs by size

Cost is hours times rate. The hour counts below are hypothetical sizes we chose to show the arithmetic; they are not benchmarks, and your own scope decides the real number. Upwork's FAQ only says that small projects "can take a few weeks, while larger projects may take several months."

Hypothetical sizeUpwork intermediate ($40 to $70)Upwork expert ($70 to $150)US employee, loaded (about $93)
200 hours (hypothetical)$8,000 to $14,000$14,000 to $30,000about $18,700
800 hours (hypothetical)$32,000 to $56,000$56,000 to $120,000about $74,700
2,000 hours (hypothetical)$80,000 to $140,000$140,000 to $300,000about $186,800

Two things the table leaves out. First, testing: BLS lists a separate median wage of $104,300 for software quality assurance analysts and testers (May 2025), so a team that adds a tester adds at least that wage, before benefits. Second, the expert column has no ceiling, because Upwork's top band reads "$150+".

The loaded cost of an in-house developer

The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook gives a median annual wage of $135,980 for software developers in May 2025. Divided over a full-time year of 2,080 hours, that is about $65.38 an hour. The handbook's wider group (developers, QA analysts and testers together) shows $64.44 an hour.

Wages are not the whole cost. In the BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation release of September 9, 2026, wages and salaries were 70.0 percent of private industry employer costs in June 2026, and benefits the other 30.0 percent. If a developer's benefits follow that average, the loaded cost is about $65.38 / 0.70 = $93 an hour, or about $194,000 a year. That is our approximation: the 70 percent is an average across all private industry jobs, and ECEC counts hours worked, not hours paid.

One developer month (2,080 / 12 = about 173 hours) at that loaded rate is about $16,200, before recruiting, equipment and software licenses, which we did not price.

Freelancer or employee: where the break-even sits

An employee is a fixed yearly cost; a freelancer is paid by the hour. On our estimate, a US developer with benefits costs about $194,000 a year. Spread over 2,080 hours that is the same $93 an hour, but only if there is a full year of work. With half a year of work, the employee's cost per useful hour roughly doubles to about $187.

That gives a simple rule of thumb from the numbers above. A freelancer billing less than about $93 an hour (all of Upwork's intermediate band, and the lower part of its expert band) costs less per hour than a fully booked US employee, before any marketplace fees. Above $93, on this estimate alone, a full year of steady work favors hiring. Short or uncertain projects favor paying by the hour, because the employee costs the same in quiet months. This leaves out what the rates do not show: management time, hiring time, and how fast each option starts.

Web app development cost

A web app is custom software that runs in the browser, so the same arithmetic applies with a different wage. BLS puts the median annual wage for web developers at $92,650 in May 2025. Our arithmetic puts that at about $44.54 an hour, or about $64 loaded on the same 70 percent assumption. A web app with back end work, user accounts and integrations may also need software developer skills, so we would budget with both rates in view. For a marketing site rather than an app, see our breakdown of website design cost; for phone apps, see app development cost, which also covers app store fees.

What pushes the price up or down

Upwork lists five cost factors on its rate page:

  • Project complexity: "More complex projects require more time and expertise."
  • Developer experience: "More experienced developers typically charge higher rates", the gap between the $20 entry band and the $150+ expert band.
  • Technology stack: "Specialized technologies can increase costs."
  • Project duration: "Longer projects may offer different rates compared to short-term tasks."
  • Location: "Developers in different regions may have varying rates."

We would add one more from the arithmetic: scope changes. Every added feature adds hours, and hours multiply by the rate, so a change that costs 50 hours costs $2,000 to $3,500 at the intermediate band (50 x $40 to 50 x $70).

Build custom or start on a white-label platform

Some projects called "custom software" are a standard stack that a platform may already cover. HighLevel's pricing page lists plans at $97, $297 and $497 a month; the $497 Pro plan includes "SaaS Mode", which the page says turns HighLevel "into your own sellable software product". A year of Pro is $5,964, about 64 loaded developer hours at $93.

That comparison is not like for like: a platform gives you its features, not yours, and you rent rather than own. We suggest building custom when the workflow is your edge or no platform does it, and starting on a platform when the need is standard and speed matters. If you do build, Upwork's own advice applies: make sure the contract says who owns the code (it says to "ensure that your contract specifies IP rights and ownership of the developed software").

How to budget a custom software build

  1. Write the scope down. List the screens, user roles, integrations and reports. Hours come from scope, so a vague scope gives a vague price.
  2. Get an hours estimate, not just a price. Ask each bidder for hours by feature, so you can compare rates and hours separately.
  3. Pick a rate band. Use the table above: $40 to $70 intermediate, $70 to $150+ expert, about $93 for a US employee with benefits.
  4. Add testing and changes. Plan for QA time and for scope changes, since both add hours.
  5. Plan for upkeep. Upwork notes that many developers offer ongoing support and maintenance. We found no primary source for a standard yearly maintenance percentage, so ask each bidder to quote it.

What we could not verify

  • GSA ceiling rates for federal software developer labor categories: the GSA pricing tool did not load when we checked.
  • A primary source for yearly maintenance as a share of build cost: none found, so we give no percentage.
  • Agency hourly rates by country: not read for this guide.
